thread:
Alex M: Quick question — do we want to compress telemetry at the SDK/edge (customer side) before sending to the collector, or leave compression upstream in the ingest plane? Thinking of trace/metric/log envelopes and cost attribution implications.

Priya S: Short take: edge compress reduces network costs but makes early sampling/enrichment harder if we need to peek into payloads for routing. Also CPU at edge varies by customer.

Marco: Agree. If we gzip at SDK, the ingest cannot do sampling-by-attribute without decompressing. That adds CPU + memory spikes on collectors.

Li Chen: Also think about partial reads for streaming. If a client sends a large compressed bundle and the connection drops, we lose the whole chunk. Uncompressed chunking allows partial stitch.

Alex M: Good points. On the other hand, uncompressed payloads increase egress costs for customers on slow links. Per-tenant compression would be ideal but introduces config surface.

Priya S: We should consider two axes: where compression happens (edge vs ingest) and the unit of compression (per-span, per-batch, per-tenant aggregate). Each has tradeoffs for latency, CPU, and enrichment semantics.

Marco: Proposed options: 
1) Always compress at ingest (collectors decompress) — simplest for pipeline observability, keeps collectors in charge.
2) Allow SDK-level compression with a header so collector knows how to handle it (Content-Encoding: gzip).
3) Hybrid: small events uncompressed, large blobs compressed.

Li Chen: For cost attribution we need stable IDs in the envelope head. If the head is compressed with body, downstream cost-attribution tasks can't index until decompress. Minimal schema change: keep metadata header plaintext and compress only the body. Example: 

```
{ "hdr": { "tenant": "acme", "billing_key": "bk_123", "schema_v": 2 },
  "body": "<gzip base64 blob>"
}
```
Then collectors can route/cost-tag without decompressing.

Marco: Nice. That also helps late-enrich: match on hdr, then lazily decompress body only when needed. Reduces overall decompress ops.

Alex M: Edge case: what about envelopes that need field-level sampling where the sampled attribute lives in the body? If we only inspect hdr we lose that. We could maintain a small sampling-index in hdr for common selectors.

Priya S: That suggests we need a compatibility contract: sdk/agent must populate a small shard of indexable attributes in hdr for all events. Backwards compat via schema_v.

infra-bot: Deploy note: collector v2.4.0 will accept Content-Encoding header and expose decompress counters to metrics. (deployed to staging) :thumbsup:

Li Chen: Performance-wise, decompress-on-demand is better than decompress-all. We should add metrics for decompress rate, CPU per-decompress, and failed-decompress count.

Marco: We also need to think about backpressure and memory. If SDK sends a compressed 50MB bundle, collector has to buffer whole thing. We should set max-envelop-size and require chunked uploads for anything > X.

Alex M: Actionable next steps I propose: 
- RFC for "hdr/body compression" contract + schema examples (Priya + Li)
- Microbench decompression latency/CPU for common compressors (gzip, brotli, zstd) on our collector instance types (Marco)
- SDK guidelines: default to no-compress for small events, compress >1MB, always include hdr fields uncompressed (Alex)
- Add collector metrics for decompress ops and envelope size histogram (infra team)

Priya S: I'll start an RFC draft and include sample envelopes + compatibility matrix. Will also call out how sampling must be supported (index fields in hdr).

Marco: I'll spin up perf runs and post results in this thread next week.

Li Chen: I'll add the max-envelope-size proposal and chunking behaviour to the RFC appendix. Also sketch failure mode: if decompress fails mark event as "body-unavailable" but still keep hdr for cost attribution.

Alex M: Awesome. Thanks team. If no objections, we'll use hdr/body split as the default pattern. Anyone want to volunteer to review the RFC before I PR?

Priya S: I'll review.

Marco: +1

infra-bot: Reminder — staging collector rollout scheduled 2026-05-03 02:00 UTC.

Alex M: Closing note — keep the SDK flag opt-in for now so we can measure uptake before rolling default.
